description: Hot and Sour Soup is a beloved classic in Chinese cuisine, known for its tantalizing balance of fiery spice and tangy vinegar. This comforting and flavorful soup is packed with an array of textures, from silky tofu to crunchy wood ear mushrooms, making every spoonful a delightful experience. It is the perfect starter or light meal, warming both the body and the soul with its complex and invigorating taste.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Begin by soaking the dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in separate bowls of hot water for at least 20 minutes until softened. Once rehydrated, remove the tough stems from the shiitake mushrooms and slice both types of mushrooms thinly. Julienne the pork loin, firm tofu, and bamboo shoots into uniform strips. In a small bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and cold water to create a smooth slurry. Beat the egg in another small bowl.

instructions.title: Simmer Broth and Pork
instructions.text: Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into a large pot or Dutch oven and bring it to a rolling boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, add the julienned pork loin (or chicken) to the broth and cook for 2-3 minutes until it is no longer pink. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Add Main Fillings
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the prepared shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and julienned tofu to the simmering broth. Stir gently to combine all ingredients and let it simmer for another 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Stir in the light soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Taste the soup and adjust the vinegar and white pepper to your preference. Remember that hot and sour soup should have a prominent tangy and spicy kick. Add salt if necessary, keeping in mind the soy sauce already adds salinity.

instructions.title: Thicken and Add Egg
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir to re-mix it, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Continue to stir until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Once thickened, slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the soup in a thin stream while gently stirring in a circular motion. This will create delicate egg ribbons.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil and, if using, the chili oil. Ladle the hot and sour soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with chopped green onions before serving immediately. Enjoy this authentic and flavorful Chinese classic.

tips: For the best texture, always add cornstarch slurry slowly while stirring continuously to avoid lumps and achieve a smooth, silky consistency.
Adjust the amount of rice vinegar and white pepper at the end to suit your personal preference for tanginess and heat. A good hot and sour soup should have a pronounced balance of both.

Hot and Sour Soup is best enjoyed fresh. If you have leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of broth or water if it has thickened too much.
article:
Hot and Sour Soup is more than just a dish; it's an experience. A cornerstone of Chinese cuisine, this beloved soup captivates with its intriguing balance of piquant, tangy, savory, and umami flavors. It’s a comforting embrace on a chilly day and a lively appetizer that awakens the palate. Originating from Sichuan and Hunan provinces, its popularity has transcended borders, becoming a staple in Chinese restaurants worldwide and a cherished dish for home cooks. If you've ever craved that perfect blend of fiery spice and zesty sourness, you're in the right place. This article will guide you through understanding, preparing, and mastering the authentic Hot and Sour Soup recipe, ensuring a delightful culinary journey into the heart of Chinese Soups and Stews.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

At its core, Hot and Sour Soup (Suan La Tang in Mandarin) is a hearty, flavorful broth thickened with cornstarch, brimming with an assortment of ingredients, and characterized by its signature "hot" (spicy) and "sour" (tangy) profile. The heat typically comes from white pepper and, optionally, chili oil, while the sourness is primarily derived from Chinese black vinegar or rice vinegar. Beyond these defining tastes, the soup offers a complex tapestry of savory notes from ingredients like soy sauce, sesame oil, and often a rich chicken or vegetable broth.

The texture is equally important – a silky, slightly viscous broth that coats the palate, studded with tender shreds of pork, delicate tofu, crunchy bamboo shoots, earthy mushrooms (like wood ear and shiitake), and delicate ribbons of egg. Each spoonful is a delightful interplay of textures and tastes, making it a truly iconic dish in the realm of Chinese Soups and Stews. It's a testament to the sophisticated flavor balancing act that defines much of Chinese cooking.

## Ingredients for Hot and Sour Soup

Crafting an authentic Hot and Sour Soup recipe requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

For the Broth Base:
*   6 cups chicken or vegetable broth (high quality makes a difference!)
*   2 tablespoons light soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon dark soy sauce (for color and depth)
*   1/4 cup rice vinegar (or Chinese black vinegar for a more complex sourness)
*   2-3 tablespoons white pepper (don't be shy, it's key to the "hot"!)
*   1 tablespoon sesame oil
*   1-2 teaspoons chili oil (optional, for extra heat)
*   Salt to taste (adjust at the end)

For the Solids:
*   4 oz lean pork, shredded (pork loin or tenderloin works well)
*   4 oz firm or silken tofu, cut into small matchsticks
*   1/2 cup bamboo shoots, shredded
*   1/2 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and shredded
*   1/4 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated, stemmed, and thinly sliced
*   2 tablespoons lily flowers (dried, rehydrated, optional but traditional)
*   2 large eggs, lightly beaten
*   2 green onions, thinly sliced (for garnish)

For the Thickener:
*   3 tablespoons cornstarch
*   4 tablespoons cold water (to make a slurry)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to bring your Hot and Sour Soup recipe to life:

1.  **Prepare Ingredients:** Rehydrate dried mushrooms and lily flowers in warm water for 20-30 minutes. Drain, squeeze out excess water, and slice thinly. Shred pork and tofu. Whisk eggs. Prepare the cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl.
2.  **Cook Pork:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring the broth to a simmer over medium heat. Add the shredded pork and cook for 2-3 minutes until it changes color and is cooked through.
3.  **Add Vegetables:** Stir in the bamboo shoots, wood ear mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, and lily flowers (if using). Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer and cook for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
4.  **Season the Soup:** Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, and a generous amount of white pepper. Stir well and taste. Adjust the sourness and pepperiness to your preference. Remember, the "hot" primarily comes from the white pepper, so don't be afraid to add more!
5.  **Thicken the Broth:** Give the cornstarch slurry a quick whisk again (it settles quickly). While the soup is at a gentle simmer, slowly pour the slurry into the soup in a thin stream, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. You might not need all of it.
6.  **Add Tofu and Egg:** Gently stir in the shredded tofu. Then, slowly pour the beaten eggs into the simmering soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction with chopsticks or a fork to create delicate egg ribbons.
7.  **Final Touches:** Remove from heat. Stir in the sesame oil and chili oil (if using). Taste one last time and adjust salt, vinegar, or white pepper as needed.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle hot into bowls, garnish with fresh green onions, and serve immediately. This Hot and Sour Soup recipe is best enjoyed fresh!

## Pro Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup

Achieving restaurant-quality Hot and Sour Soup at home is entirely possible with a few key techniques and considerations:

*   **Don't Skimp on White Pepper:** This is arguably the most crucial ingredient for the "hot" component of the soup. While chili oil adds heat, the unique pungency of white pepper is what defines authentic Hot and Sour Soup. Start with the recommended amount and add more to taste.
*   **Balance is Key:** The beauty of this soup lies in the perfect equilibrium between hot, sour, and savory. Taste often as you go, especially after adding vinegar and white pepper. You want each flavor to shine without overpowering the others.
*   **Cornstarch Slurry Technique:** Ensure your slurry is lump-free. Pour it slowly into the simmering soup while stirring constantly. If the soup gets too thick, you can always thin it with a little more broth or water. If it's not thick enough, prepare a small additional slurry.
*   **Egg Ribbons:** For delicate, wispy egg strands, pour the beaten egg slowly into the simmering soup from a slight height, stirring gently in a circular motion with chopsticks or a fork. Avoid vigorous stirring, which can break up the ribbons.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Using good quality broth, fresh tofu, and authentic Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar is excellent) will elevate your Hot and Sour Soup recipe significantly.

## Serving Suggestions

Hot and Sour Soup is incredibly versatile. It makes a fantastic appetizer for any Chinese meal, pairing beautifully with dishes like General Tso's chicken, Kung Pao shrimp, or vegetable lo mein. It can also be a light yet satisfying meal on its own, especially when packed with extra proteins and vegetables. Garnish with additional chopped green onions, a drizzle of extra chili oil for those who like it spicier, or even a sprinkle of fresh cilantro for an added layer of freshness. Some enjoy a dash of extra vinegar at the table to customize the sourness to their liking.

## Variations and Substitutions

This Hot and Sour Soup recipe is remarkably adaptable, allowing for numerous variations to suit dietary preferences or ingredient availability:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Omit the pork and use vegetable broth. Increase the amount of tofu and mushrooms for a heartier soup. Ensure any chili oil used is vegetarian. This makes for an equally delicious plant-based Hot and Sour Soup recipe.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork, you can use shredded chicken breast or thigh, or even small shrimp. Add shrimp towards the end of cooking as they cook quickly.
*   **Additional Vegetables:** Feel free to incorporate other thinly sliced vegetables like carrots, water chestnuts, snow peas, or even spinach for added color and nutrients.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of white pepper and chili oil to your heat tolerance. For extra kick, a few slices of fresh bird's eye chili can be added.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Use tamari instead of regular soy sauce to make the soup gluten-free. Ensure your broth and other sauces are also gluten-free.
*   **Broth Flavor:** While chicken broth is common, a rich mushroom broth or even a pork bone broth can add incredible depth.

Mastering this Hot and Sour Soup recipe is a rewarding culinary achievement, offering a delicious and comforting dish that truly embodies the spirit of Chinese Soups and Stews. Whether you stick to the classic or experiment with variations, you're sure to enjoy this tantalizing bowl of flavor.
